mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.0% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher borrowing costs depressing equity valuation multiples.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5.0 and prev(FEDFUNDS) > 5.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 60-day window mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by at least 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a strengthening labor market, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > prev(PAYEMS) * 1.02 AND UNRATE < prev(UNRATE) - 0.5 in the same month
failure_condition: In at least 60% of triggered months, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as it indicates robust economic momentum supporting equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > prev(INDPRO) * 1.02 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 50 such triggers, the average 5-day forward return is not significantly positive (mean < 0.5% with 95% CI including zero).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3.0% and a rise in retail sales (HOUST) by at least 2% are jointly associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days, reflecting improved demand conditions.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 3.0 AND HOUST > prev(HOUST) * 1.02 in the same month
failure_condition: In 40% or more of such events, the 20-day forward return is negative or flat (≤ 0%).

mechanism_narrative: During a 3-month period of accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.3% for three months), the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to preemptive rate hikes that dampen equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth > 0.3 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative 60-day forward return occurs in 80% of such inflationary windows (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for two consecutive months without a corresponding rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5 AND prev(UNRATE) ≥ 3.5 for two consecutive months AND PAYEMS ≤ prev(PAYEMS) in both months
regime_hint: labor market tightening without participation expansion
failure_condition: In 70% of such triggered periods, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals a deepening supply-side weakness and risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prev(INDPRO) * 0.97 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 100 such contractions, the average 5-day forward return is not negative (mean ≥ 0.1% with 95% CI including zero).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4.0%, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as investors anticipate rate cuts and improved credit conditions.
failure_condition: In 60% of such events, the 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (mean ≤ 0.2% with 95% CI including zero).
